neighbours.label: a comma interrupting a verb of saying/knowing before its 'that' clause ('noted, however, that'; 'We all know, and ...')
fire: The inspectors reported, however, that the bridge needed urgent repairs.
Everyone in the village knows, of course, that the mill closed years ago.
I have come to believe, after much thought, that the plan cannot work.
The study's authors admit, nonetheless, that the sample was rather small.
She later discovered, to her surprise, that the letter had never been sent.
It must be stressed, at this point, that no one was seriously hurt.
The minister insisted, once again, that taxes would not be raised.
We now understand, thanks to new scans, that the tumour had shrunk.
quiet: The inspectors reported that the bridge needed urgent repairs before winter.
Everyone in the village knows that the mill closed many years ago.
After much thought, I have come to the view that the plan cannot work.
The study's authors admit that the sample was rather small for a trial.
To her surprise, the letter she found had never actually been sent.
At this point, the doctors were relieved that no one was seriously hurt.
Once again, the minister repeated that taxes would not be raised.
Thanks to new scans, the doctors now see that the tumour had shrunk.

notes: card: ',' x20 right after 'know', 'realise', 'said', 'find out', 'noted' with the that-clause postponed; + pole is the subject of a complement clause right after 'found/told us'. Probe: 'observed, however, that' 0.23; without comma 0.01. Near misses: same verbs without the interruption, and commas in other roles.
